episode_title: 1205. Pause in His Law Career Sent Him in the Right Direction

real_qa.q: Why did Jimmy Jenkins leave his criminal law career in New York City to return to Florida?
real_qa.r: His father was diagnosed with late-stage prostate cancer in the late 1990s, and Jenkins felt obligated to help his mother who was serving as the sole caregiver. As an only child, he returned to Florida to assist. When 9/11 happened while his family was adjusting to life back in Florida, Jenkins and his wife decided not to return to New York City, fearing the danger it posed to their children.

real_qa.q: What is the main focus of Jimmy Jenkins' children's book I'm a Farm Crop Too?
real_qa.r: Jenkins is writing a children's book with the working title I'm a Farm Crop Too about hemp as a farm crop. He wanted to educate children and adults about how hemp can be beneficial and productive, and how it has been used for thousands of years despite being vilified and discredited over the years.
real_qa.requete: I'm a Farm Crop Too hemp children's book

real_qa.q: What role did Samuel Hunter play in shaping Jimmy Jenkins' intellectual development?
real_qa.r: Samuel Hunter was a family friend and educator who owned a fruit grove in Vero Beach and was very scientifically minded in his growing philosophies. He taught Jenkins about lunar projections and their impact on irrigation and grove management, which piqued Jenkins' curiosity about scientific thinking and forecasting using data and information at hand.
real_qa.requete: Samuel Hunter fruit grove lunar projections farming

real_qa.q: Why did Jimmy Jenkins decide not to obtain a Florida law license after moving back to the state?
real_qa.r: Jenkins deliberately avoided obtaining a Florida law license because he recognized that if he got licensed, he would chase the brass ring like putting a bone in front of a dog—meaning he would fall back into the hot shot trial lawyer lifestyle he was trying to escape. Instead, he pursued a position as a lawyer editor at a small publishing company in Leon County.
real_qa.requete: Jimmy Jenkins Florida law license lawyer editor

real_qa.q: What insight did Jimmy Jenkins gain while caring for his father about work and family priorities?
real_qa.r: While taking care of his father, Jenkins realized he had missed a lot of life chasing career success. He understood that his overwhelming need to be the provider had caused him to miss significant time with his parents, extended family, wife, and children. This led him to fundamentally reevaluate what he was working for and why, recognizing that only 34% of people in the United States are satisfied with their work according to Gallup's 35-year study.

guest.bio_context: Jimmy Jenkins earned his law degree from the University of Maryland and worked as a criminal prosecutor for several years before transitioning to private criminal defense practice in New York City. He later relocated to Florida and shifted his career focus toward writing and publishing, authoring Green Rush Fever about his family's entry into the Florida hemp industry in 2019. His parents were both educators in the Indian River County school system—his mother a school librarian and his father a school teacher and counselor.

real_quote: There was a lot of life that I had missed chasing the brass ring by going to law school and pushing on to New York City, and I realized I had missed a lot of time with my parents and extended family, even with my own wife and children.
